items.title: Alphabet 旗下药物 AI 企业 Isomorphic Labs 完成 50 亿美元 C 轮融资
items.description: IT之家 11 月 17 日消息，由诺贝尔奖得主 Demis Hassabis（戴米斯 · 哈萨比斯）领导的 Alphabet 旗下 AI 赋能药物研发企业 Isomorphic Labs 当地时间今日宣布， 其完成了总额 50 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 333.96 亿元人民币） 的 C 轮融资 。 本轮融资由 Greenoaks 和 Sequoia Capital 共同领投，a16z (Andreessen Horowitz) 等新投资者加入，Alphabet 持续投入大量资金，Thrive Capital、MGX、GV、CapitalG、淡马锡、英国主权 AI 基金等现有投资者也参与了融资。 Isomorphic Labs 计划利用这笔资金继续 推进基础模拟模型的发展 ， 扩大内部及合作药物候选项目的规模 ，并 建设全球 AI 驱动的生物工程基础设施 。

items.title: 亚马逊 AWS 将向黑石出售并回租 50 亿美元数据中心资产

items.description: IT之家 11 月 17 日消息，米哈游旗下《崩坏》系列 AI 研发团队现已公布通用视觉语言动作基础模型“Gamer”。该模型能够模拟真人操作方式自主游玩 3D 和 2D 游戏。 根据研究论文及项目页面公开的信息，Gamer 无需读取游戏内部数据，也不依赖游戏专用 API，而是通过每秒 5 帧（5 Hz）的频率采集游戏画面作为输入，再生成相当于 30 Hz 的原生键盘按键状态及鼠标移动指令，从而模拟真人使用键鼠操作游戏的过程。 为了解决长时间执行任务时面临的内存限制和推理延迟问题，研究团队利用超过 1 万小时的跨游戏键鼠操作轨迹进行持续预训练，并结合稀疏思维指令微调和时序感知强化学习优化模型。此外，团队还专门开发了名为“Streaming-vLLM”的推理引擎。在 NVIDIA H200 硬件环境下，该引擎将端到端请求延迟从 1306 毫秒大幅降低至 65.12 毫秒。 研究团队还展示了 Gamer 在《崩坏：星穹铁道》中执行主线任务、探索场景及完成解谜挑战的实机演示。测试数据显示，经过强化学习训练的 Gamer-RL 在 40 项此前未接触过的小游戏任务中，平均成功率达到 49.7%

items.author: Ram Iyer
items.content: Isomorphic Labs , the AI drug-discovery platform that was spun out of Google’s DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 billion in a Series C funding round as it seeks to take its drug candidates to clinical trials. The funding was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with new investor Andreessen Horowitz and other investors also participating. All of the company’s existing backers, including Alphabet’s venture divisions GV and Capital G, Thrive Capital, MGX, Temasek, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund, also invested. Isomorphic Labs builds an AI drug-design engine that uses a slew of simulation AI models that explore various areas of chemistry to help the company design drugs. The company, whose work builds on DeepMind’s breakthrough AlphaFold protein-folding AI model , said its program has yielded “positive preclinical results” in oncology and immunology. The lab has struck deals with pharma giants like Eli Lilly, Novartis, and Johnson & Johnson. The new funding, which comes on the heels of a $2.1 billion Series B round in May, will be used to continue developing its drug-design engine, as well as to foray into more types of medicine. The Series C is Isomorphic’s first fundraise since its founder and CEO, Demis Hassabis, left his position as head of DeepMind to focus on drug discovery, which also saw him moving into a chairman role at DeepMind. items.title: Science Corporation’s brain tech is worth $3.5 billion after new funding
items.description: Science Corp raised a $400 million Series D to scale up its anti-blindness business.
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: Science Corporation , the medical technology start-up founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak in 2021, raised a $400 million Series D, the company said in a blog post . Investors in the new round valued the company at $3.5 billion, a person familiar with the deal told TechCrunch. Those backers included Khosla Ventures, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Tenet Healthcare, 885 Capital, Y Combinator, and PLC Neurotech. Hodak, who talked his way into a graduate neuroscience lab as a college student and has pursued biotechnology ever since, co-founded Science to leverage new technologies to understand and interact with the brain. Science’s first product is PRIMA, a wearable and implantable chip that helps people with age-related macular degeneration recover some vision. The device is approved in Europe and available in Germany, as well as being trialled for new conditions. Hodak announced that the device is now being trialled for patients with another blindness-causing condition, Stargardt’s disease, while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt. With the funding, the company aims to bring the device to the United States through the FDA’s Humanitarian Device Exemption, which lets experimental medical technology be used to treat rare conditions. Science has convinced the FDA that advanced macular degeneration in both eyes is uncommon enough to let them seek approval to use the device on people in the US.

items.author: Kirsten Korosec
items.content: Nvidia has formed a committee to oversee national security policies and export control compliance following the abrupt resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who had links to one of the company’s customers. Nvidia said Tuesday that the new standing committee will give board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks. The move comes amid increased scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Huang’s alleged ties to the suspected spy and his advocacy for easing restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China. The Commerce Department said Monday it was planning to introduce new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside of the U.S. in an effort to prevent companies in China and elsewhere from circumventing existing rules by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries. The interim rule was made in direct response to the unfolding chip smuggling scandal at Nvidia. The announcement comes just a few hours before Nvidia’s highly anticipated third-quarter earnings call. Analysts, the media, and shareholders expect the company to address the controversy and outline how it might affect operations. This is the first major action by the company under the leadership of Collette Kress, the company’s CFO who took over as interim CEO after Huang stepped down last week. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue. The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP , a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js , the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled. Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin , as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Altman made his first public comments about Huang’s departure on Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, where he also discussed topics ranging from data center pushback to recursive self-improvement. Numerous executives and members of the AI industry have argued for Nvidia to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, who were among the signatories in a public letter. Many fear that Huang’s departure may cause Nvidia to rethink the enormous financial risks it has taken that have fueled the AI boom. Huang is also reportedly setting up a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return. When asked whether he thought Huang should return to the company, Altman said: “I don’t think I know enough to answer that question.”

items.title: FBI says Artex AI open source hacking tool used to breach networks in ‘under three hours’
items.description: The FBI says that the open source hacking tool was used in cyberattacks targeting a U.S. IT giant and the South Korean financial industry.
items.author: Zack Whittaker
items.content: The FBI is warning that hackers are relying on autonomous AI hacking tools to launch cyberattacks across the U.S. and globally. The campaigns include a widespread hack of customers of American IT company ConnectWise and across South Korea’s financial industry. In its latest flash cybersecurity advisory , the FBI says hackers have targeted several industries in recent months, including financial services, government, tech, defense, phone and internet companies, and law firms, using open source tools like Artex to carry out autonomous-driven cyberattacks. Artex is one of several open source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network’s defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI says Artex intrusions can be “noisy,” meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company’s defensive alerts. But the tools allow hackers to move at speeds that make it far more difficult for human defenders to keep up. items.author: Connie Loizos
items.content: Years ago, as questions mounted about WeWork’s soaring valuation, I sat down with co-founder Adam Neumann. We were negotiating a stage interview, and he asked to meet me twice in the weeks leading up to it, once at a WeWork in San Francisco and again at his office in New York. I knew full well that the numbers that SoftBank in particular had assigned to WeWork made little sense , but I came away understanding why investors wanted to throw in their lot with him. It’s similarly easy to understand why people are enchanted by Jordan Belfort, the self-proclaimed “Wolf of Wall Street.” Belfort famously pleaded guilty in 1999 to securities fraud and money laundering tied to Stratton Oakmont, the Long Island brokerage where salespeople pushed penny stocks in pump-and-dump schemes while Belfort acquired a Southampton mansion, a 167-foot yacht, and at least one helicopter. (He destroyed the latter two while high on quaaludes and cocaine, as depicted in Martin Scorsese’s famous adaptation of Belfort’s autobiography, “The Wolf of Wall Street.”) You might think someone who spent 22 months in prison and was ordered to pay $110.4 million in restitution to 1,513 victims wouldn’t get another shake. items.title: OpenAI releases a new image classifier and ChatGPT warnings to combat CSAM
items.description: ChatGPT will ban an account trying to access CSAM content for 24 hours as a warning.
items.author: Ivan Mehta
items.content: OpenAI today announced new tools to combat child sexual abuse material (CSAM) amid growing safety concerns around the use of AI tools. These features include a new image classifier to detect CSAM, warnings and temporary blocks to prevent users from creating or accessing content that sexualizes children, a new guideline for developers, and a set of tools for law enforcement. The company unveiled a new image classifier that can detect CSAM images, including the ones generated by AI. OpenAI is giving select companies access to its classifier through its API at no cost. The tool looks for visual signs of abuse in images not seen before and assigns a score that can give an indicative direction to reviewers about dealing with CSAM. OpenAI said that it developed this classifier with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), and it is working with Tech Coalition and ROOST to share access to the tool. In its early testing with partners, the AI company found that the classifier flags 48% fewer images while finding the same number of abusive images, reducing the work of reviewers. Plus, images flagged by the classifier are twice as likely to be abusive images. items.title: Audible turns to AI to help users discover audiobooks
items.description: Audible's new AI-generated audio previews summarize a book's themes and what readers liked about it, in addition to playing the narrated sample.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: Amazon-owned audiobook service Audible is turning to AI to help listeners find their next book. The company on Monday launched a new “audio discovery” feature that provides a brief overview of a book’s themes and a summary of what readers liked about it, as well as commentary from an Audible editor or an author, in addition to playing the narrated sample. The overview audio itself is generated using AI, and the commentary is pulled from recordings of past Audible interviews, the company says. The idea is that this type of expanded introduction to a story could help users decide what to listen to next, particularly when they’re on the go and don’t have time to scroll through comments or reviews. The feature follows last month’s launch of a handful of AI tools that let users engage more with the story, interact with characters, or catch up with the help of recaps. These features have come as Audible faces new competition in the audiobooks market, namely from Spotify, which introduced audiobook listening hours as part of its paid subscriptions. That service expanded last month to over 180 markets. Audible’s new feature takes a cue from how Amazon is already using AI to help people shop: On the Amazon storefront, AI can summarize buyers’ product reviews so shoppers can get a quick sense of what people had to say, as well as the pros and cons of a particular item. items.title: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely
items.description: Under the interim rule, the U.S. will require firms to get licenses to export AI chips if they may provide compute to China or other restricted countries.
items.author: Ram Iyer
items.content: The Trump administration on Monday is preparing to roll out new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside the U.S., seeking to prevent companies, especially those in China, from getting past U.S. export controls by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries. Under the interim rule , the Commerce Department will require companies to get licenses to export, reexport, or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if they may provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries. The remote-access rules target companies based in the U.S.’s D:5 group of embargoed countries, which includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and 18 others. The U.S. already has rules requiring chip companies to get a license to ship AI chips to companies based in, or owned by any business in, this group of countries. “This new control is a logical extension of existing controls,” the interim rule reads. “These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models.” The move comes days after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy linked to one of the chipmaker’s customers. items.description: You could use Ask Maps to plan a holiday shopping day trip or something more complex, like a three-day road trip featuring coastal hikes and oceanfront dining.
items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: Google announced on Monday that it’s rolling out new Maps features that are designed to help people plan trips and everyday tasks using AI. The company is launching the ability for Maps to create trip itineraries and find appointments for users. The new features reflect a broader shift in how tech companies are positioning AI, which is less as a tool that just answers questions and more as an assistant that can complete tasks on users’ behalf. While many companies have released AI agents to complete these tasks, Google is working to bring that approach into a service that millions of people already use every day. Google says users can use the navigation platform’s “Ask Maps” tool to build step-by-step trip itineraries and get real-time details about their route right when they pull up directions. For example, you could use Ask Maps to plan a holiday shopping day trip or something more complex, like a three-day road trip featuring coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Google says. You’ll get a day-by-day itinerary with insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop. Once you’re happy with your itinerary, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop. When you’re ready to head out, you can use Ask Maps to reopen your itinerary or find the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. items.title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
items.description: Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries, with some businesses switching from established CRMs.
items.author: Jagmeet Singh
items.content: Dreamteam , a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge. The funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation. Traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring. Salespeople spent considerable time updating records, yet managers still struggled to get a reliable picture of their business. “In all these years, I have never come across an instance where I could click a button and get a forecast from the CRM,” he said. items.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
items.description: Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions.
items.author: Ivan Mehta
items.content: Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people. The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.
